Within a single evaluation, the two are distinguished by whether the panel's errors are structured (indicating missing causal links) or random (indicating noise the checklist does not address).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the evaluation's sample size is insufficient to distinguish structured from random error patterns, the test is inconclusive.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task itself has no stable causal structure (pure noise tasks), neither type of checklist can be genuinely reliable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is a hybrid (partly causal, partly correlational), error structure may be ambiguous and the test fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A causal-model checklist encodes the generative structure of correct judgment: each step corresponds to a real dependency in the task. A correlational checklist encodes surface regularities without generative structure: errors are random relative to task structure because the checklist has no model to break. In a single evaluation, error structure is diagnostic: structured errors imply a causal model (genuine); random errors imply a correlation filter (coincidence).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
